title: Mitigate scheduler drain oscillation causing hidden queue saturation & KV-cache thrash
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Customer escalations indicate intermittent, high 95th/99th token-latency spikes for long-context requests on Dedicated and Private deployments. Root cause appears to be an interaction between the continuous-batching scheduler's drain behavior and per-tenant admission bursts: the scheduler oscillates between aggressive drains and backlogged admission windows, causing a hidden queue to build and triggers KV-cache eviction churn which amplifies token-serving latency.
background: Escalation came from two customers (financial-analytics and health-qa) after infra upgrades in mid-February. Symptoms: sudden tail-latency spikes (5x baseline at p99), increased token-generation time for sequences >8k tokens, and transient increase in cache-miss rate. A previous mitigation (raising global admission cap) temporarily hid the problem but increased cost and reduced fairness for small requests.
reproduction_steps: Run mixed-length workload (70% short <256 tokens, 30% long 6k-12k tokens) targeting a Dedicated pool with 8x A100s.
Enable continuous batching + default drain interval (50ms) and admission windowing.
Generate microbursts of concurrent long requests (10-20 simultaneous).
Observe sustained p99 token latency and KV-cache eviction rate on the serving hosts.
Compare with same workload after applying soft per-tenant admission cap (see temporary mitigation).
investigation_notes: 03-02: Collected traces from affected customers (trace ids sent to SRE). Observed repeated drain cycles where scheduler drains many small batches then stalls when large requests re-enter admission.
03-03: Heap/profile of KV store shows eviction spikes coincident with drain completion; hot KV shards thrash when admission bursts restart.
03-04: Simulated in staging with deterministic replay harness; reproduced scheduler oscillation by injecting jitter into request arrivals. Confirmed fairness regression under mixed-length load.
03-06: Reviewed scheduler commit history — a change to 'drain-to-empty' optimization reduced transient batching latency but made admission windows more bursty under contention.
03-08: Customer impact analysis: timeouts in orchestration layer and increased retry storms for some SDK flows. Business risk high for regulated customers on Dedicated/Private.
03-10: Concluded root cause is coupling between drain policy and the admission reservoir refill logic; KV-cache thrash is secondary but amplifies latency.
03-12: Reproduced an exploit case where a sequence of overlapping long requests can starve small latency-sensitive requests by repeatedly forcing expensive KV recomputations.
temporary_mitigation: Emergency config pushed to affected Dedicated pools: enable 'soft-per-tenant-admission-cap=conservative' and increase drain-interval to 120ms (rolled back in 48h after monitoring).
Added an SLO-safe fallback to route new long requests to a lower-priority pool when admission window exceeds 60% occupancy.
Updated customer-runbooks and support playbook: how to toggle admission caps and monitor kv-cache-miss-rate.
Alert: new p95 token-latency alert and kv-cache-eviction-rate alert created (alerts/dashboard links below).
code_changes: Introduce 'drain-jitter' to spread drain completions across ticks instead of synchronized drains (impl in scheduler module).
Add per-tenant soft admission cap that decays over 500ms to avoid sudden refill bursts.
Make KV-cache eviction policy 'hot-key-protect' to reduce churn for long-lived prefix caches.
Instrument admission reservoir with fine-grained telemetry (per-tenant occupancy, last-drain-time).

rollout_plan: Canary on 10% of Dedicated pools with mixed-length synthetic load for 24h.
Monitor p50/p95/p99 and kv-cache eviction rate; abort on 20% regression at p95 for customer-facing tenants.
If canary stable, ramp to 50% over 12h, then full rollout over 48h with 2h observation windows between steps.
Provide customer-facing note and option to opt-out of new scheduler behavior for next 7 days via support config flag.
qa_checks: End-to-end deterministic replay in staging with varying long/short mixes (0/25/50/75% long).
Chaos test: introduce arrival jitter and emulate node-level GC pauses to ensure no regressions in fairness.
Load test for KV-cache: verify hot-key protection reduces eviction spikes by >=70% under long-request bursts.
Regression test: ensure small latency-sensitive requests maintain p95 within 1.2x baseline under mixed load.
next_steps: Finalize code PRs and complete peer review (assigned reviewers: Priya R., Marco L.).
Complete canary rollout and capture telemetry for 72h before ramping.
Follow-up ticket for long-term admission policy redesign (decouple refill from drain) - link Q2 roadmap.
Schedule cross-team retro with SRE, SDK, and Customer Success to capture learnings and update runbooks.
